finalMessage: Two rules fit these six nouns equally well. The ending could depend on the noun's last sound (-na after a vowel: rezu, zanjopo, ime; -ta after a consonant: mungas, repuk, azok), or each noun could belong to a lexical class that takes -na or -ta. These six forms cannot tell the two analyses apart, so I have not drafted either; neither is established. One vowel-final noun that takes -ta, or a consonant-final noun that takes -na, would settle it.
